newsitem.title: USA: Consumer credit rises again in November.
newsitem.headline: Consumer credit rises again in November.

text.p: Consumers went further into debt in November, the Federal Reserve said Wednesday, as borrowings from autos loans to credit card charges grew.
The central bank said consumer credit outstanding grew $7.4 billion to a seasonally adjusted $1.19 trillion in November, a 7.4 percent annual growth rate.
Credit grew a revised $6.5 billion in October.

The report on credit comes amid signs the economy was strengthening as last year drew to a close with most analysts forecasting that fourth quarter growth would outpace the 2.1 percent rate of growth in the third quarter.
"It suggests the household sector still feels favourably disposed to its financial position and willing to take on more debt," said Michael Moran of Daiwa Securities.
He said the new data was consistent with the healthy job market, consumer confidence and the strong stock market.
Consumer spending is closely watched by government and private economists since it fuels about two-thirds of economic activity.
The Fed said auto credit rose $500 million in November at a 1.5 percent annual rate after being up $1 billion in October.
Revolving or credit-card debt grew $3.2 billion at an 8.5 percent annual rate, compared with an $1.4 billion October advance.
Other credit, including consumer bank loans but not mortgages, grew by $3.6 billion at a 12.3 percent annual rate in November after rising $4.1 billion.
The department had previously said total consumer credit rose by $2.2 billion in October.
